_comment: The rule-carrier registry — proposal 0027, `a reduced rule stays reduced`.
A rule an incident REDUCED to one carrier is registered here with the spellings its other
carriers used. Those spellings may then appear only in the carrier, or beside a citation of it.
This registry covers ONLY the rules listed below. Every other rule in this repository is
unregistered and therefore uncovered, and nothing can audit that — a rule has no token, which is
proposal 0020's theorem. The arrears are named rather than pretended away.
`scope` and `exclude` are path PREFIXES, not globs. `exclude` wins, and the list below is the

one carrier of what it covers — read it rather than a description of it. Much of the record layer is on it, because a record legitimately quotes retired sentences forever; NOT all of it is, and which paths belong there is #367.

rules.summary: What CI runs is the set the workspace manifest YIELDS — its own declared recipes plus those its composed packs contribute, namespaced by pack — and not the list it declares. Landed at milestone 7 session 5; cli/recipe-set.mjs is the one carrier of the set and CI calls it rather than enumerating a manifest.
rules._tells_comment: Every tell below was MEASURED against the pre-sweep tree (27705ae), not invented. Two plural variants were written from memory, matched nothing, and the dead-tell audit rejected them on its first run — `invented is a claim`, and the audit is what makes that checkable rather than a maxim.

rules.summary: The A/B clause's subject is the mandates core SHIPS that an arm actually receives — the kernel's, plus the artifact mandates reachable in a built arm — of which the judgement-only rows are a part. Widened 2026-08-28 on the maintainer's ruling, from a narrower reading that named the judgement rows alone. The narrower reading could not survive measurement: `vendor --host` carries `core/skills/` not at all, so all five judgement rows reach nothing in a vendored arm.
rules._tells_comment: Every tell below was verified against 39175b50 THROUGH `normalise()` ITSELF, which is the only instrument that answers the question the audit asks. The constraint a tell must satisfy is CONTIGUITY AFTER NORMALISATION: `normalise` collapses every whitespace run to one space and strips emphasis, code markers and link markup, so a tell may span a prose line-wrap freely — but NOT a `# ` comment prefix, and NOT a string-literal boundary, because those survive normalisation and break the run. TWO EARLIER MEASUREMENTS OF THIS WERE WRONG, and the sequence is the lesson. A first cut registered four sentence-level spellings; the pre-commit checkpoint measured two of them dead, which was CORRECT. Re-measuring with `git grep -F` then reported three dead and I believed it over the checkpoint — but `git grep` is LINE-BASED and the scanner is not, so the wrong instrument produced a false correction of a right verdict. Measured through `normalise`: the `evals/README.md` and `docs/milestones/m08.md` spellings were ALIVE (the latter spans a Markdown wrap, which normalisation closes); the `cli/skill-goldens.mjs` and `.portulan/verify/skill-goldens.sh` ones were dead, across an `io.log` literal boundary and a `# ` wrap. A FIFTH spelling exists at .portulan/handoffs/2026-08-26-b-the-denominator-was-a-set-the-author-drew.md and is deliberately NOT registered: it sits under a globally excluded path where it can never be a finding, so a tell for it would buy nothing.
rules._coverage_comment: WHAT THIS RULE DOES NOT COVER, stated because the sentence it replaced overclaimed — and then overclaimed again in its first correction. `exclude` is global and lists EXACTLY: .portulan/handoffs/, .portulan/proposals/, this file, docs/milestones/, docs/plan.md and CHANGELOG.md. Those are outside every rule here, and docs/milestones/ is precisely where the fourth carrier sat and survived a sweep. NOT excluded, and a first draft of this comment wrongly implied they were by saying `the record layer`: .portulan/tasks/ and .portulan/memory/ ARE scanned, though cli/version-carriers.mjs's RECORD_PREFIXES counts both as record layer. Whether that divergence is intended is not this rule's to settle and is filed rather than assumed. So this registration stops a fifth carrier appearing IN THE REGISTERED SCOPE; it cannot see one appearing where the fourth was. Nor does the dead-tell audit protect this rule the way it protects rule 1: the carrier quotes all four spellings, so every tell stays alive whatever the citing files do, and the audit can only redden if somebody edits the carrier's own list. That is a trade, not a feature.
